episodes.title: Week 9 Trench & Scheme Preview: Bosa + Buckner Debut vs. Klint Kubiak's Raiders
episodes.topic: Week 9 LV @ SF Matchup (SF -9.5), Raheem Morris Stunt Geometry & Maxx Crosby Protection Plan

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Welcome into 49ers Faithful. Sunday afternoon on FOX at Levi's Stadium, the 6-1 Niners come out of the Week 8 bye holding the number one seed in the NFC—opening at eight and a half and steamed to minus 9.5 with a 51.5 total against the 4-4 Las Vegas Raiders. And for the first time since Week 2, Nick Bosa is off the injury designation list and cleared to hunt alongside DeForest Buckner and Osa Odighizuwa.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: The math behind defensive coordinator Raheem Morris's front is staggering, Marcus. Even without Bosa from Weeks 3 through 7, Osa Odighizuwa kept interior disruption afloat. Now Morris drops six-foot-seven DeForest Buckner into the three-technique next to Odighizuwa, with Bosa and Keion White on the Wide-9 edges. Opposing centers cannot slide protection toward Bosa without leaving Buckner singled up on a guard.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Exactly. And look across the sideline at who calls plays for Las Vegas: first-year Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak, who spent all of 2023 inside Kyle Shanahan's building as our Passing Game Specialist. Kubiak marries outside zone with Ashton Jeanty to deep play-action crossers for Kirk Cousins and Brock Bowers—the exact route spacing Raheem Morris, Fred Warner, and Deommodore Lenoir disguise split-safety rotations against every week.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Plus San Francisco enters with a plus-seven-day rest advantage coming off the bye. Under Shanahan since 2017, when QB1 is healthy post-bye, the 49ers average plus 0.21 EPA per play on their opening fifteen scripted snaps, and Brock Purdy sits among the NFL leaders at plus 63.23 passing EPA, plus 4.25 percent completion percentage over expected, and just a 3.2 percent sack rate.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: The one game-wrecker we have to neutralize for sixty minutes is Maxx Crosby. Whenever he flips away from Trent Williams to align over right tackle Colton McKivitz, watch for 21-personnel chip-and-release help from George Kittle and Kyle Juszczyk, paired with quick rhythm throws to Brandin Cooks, Jordan Watkins, and Jacob Cowing—plus newly activated Demarcus Robinson off IR.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Neutralize Crosby on third-and-medium, keep Bosa on a smart 45-snap pitch count in his return, and the implied market projection of SF 30.5 to LV 21.0 tracks right on the numbers.

episodes.title: 2026–2028 Salary Cap Blueprint: Why $35.16M Must Roll Into 2027's -$31.54M Horizon
episodes.topic: OverTheCap Multi-Year Ledger, CBA Article 13 Rollover Bridge & Brandon Aiyuk Post-June 1 Mechanics

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Let's open the live OverTheCap multi-year ledger, because the biggest misconception around the 49ers right now is treating San Francisco's 35.16 million dollars in 2026 cap space like free money. When you flip one tab forward to 2027, San Francisco is currently projected 31.54 million dollars over an estimated 327 million dollar cap ceiling.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Connect those two numbers, Elena. That explains immediately why John Lynch and Paraag Marathe refuse to take on bloated multi-year contracts this week.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Precisely. Under Article 13 of the NFL Collective Bargaining Agreement, every unused dollar of 2026 cap space rolls over one-for-one into 2027. Brock Purdy carries a 23.71 million dollar cap number this season while Nick Bosa sits at 22.99 million before both contracts escalate sharply next spring. Rolling roughly 28 to 31 million dollars forward erases almost the entire 2027 deficit without touching aging veteran restructures.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Now layer in Brandon Aiyuk meeting with team brass at SAP Performance Facility seeking reinstatement as both sides work toward a clean offseason exit.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Any trade or release executed after June first—including right now in November—functions under Post-June-1 accounting: only the current 2026 bonus proration stays on this year's cap, while remaining unamortized bonus proration accelerates onto the 2027 dead-money ledger. Structuring a bilateral settlement on unaccrued guarantees is critical so Aiyuk's exit does not compound that 31.54 million dollar 2027 crunch.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Which makes hitting on cost-controlled rookie-scale contributors—Mykel Williams, Upton Stout, Renardo Green, Dominick Puni, Gracen Halton, and Romello Height—the structural engine keeping this championship window open.

episodes.title: Nov 10 Trade Window & Calibrated 34.5% NFC #1 Seed Outlook
episodes.topic: Ranked Positional Needs, 9/18ths Rental Purchasing Power, 6-Pick 2027 Draft Ledger & Empirical-Bayes Playoff Odds

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: We are inside the final stretch before Tuesday's November 10th, 1 PM Pacific NFL Trade Deadline. John Lynch already sent our 2027 fourth-round pick to Indianapolis to bring DeForest Buckner back home alongside Osa Odighizuwa. Looking strictly at the tape and injury wire, what are San Francisco's true ranked needs?

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Number one is perimeter receiver and 12-personnel move tight end—with six receivers on reserve or restricted lists, targeting rookie-contract separators like Adonai Mitchell on the Jets, Josh Downs in Indianapolis, Rashod Bateman in Baltimore, or Greg Dulcich from Miami. Number two is left guard pass-protection stability next to Trent Williams, like Kingsley Suamataia. Number three is rotational speed edge—where winless Los Angeles Chargers veteran Khalil Mack is an ideal expiring one-year rental—followed by dime corner depth like Donte Jackson.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: And let's clear up the cap and draft math on those targets. With 35.16 million dollars in 2026 space and nine eighteenths of the regular season remaining, do the 49ers ever need a seller to eat salary?

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Not at all—and getting that direction right matters. Because signing bonus proration stays with the seller and acquiring teams only absorb nine eighteenths of remaining 2026 base salary, San Francisco actually holds over 65 million dollars in annualized base-salary purchasing power right now. Our real constraints are next year's 31.54 million dollar cap deficit and owning just 6 total picks in the 2027 draft after trading our fourth-rounder for Buckner. That means targeting expiring rentals or cheap rookie deals for Day-3 picks, while steering clear of zero-sack age-37 traps like Cameron Jordan or extended starters like Michael Mayer.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Now connect that deadline discipline to our calibrated ten-thousand-run NFC playoff model, Elena—because raw un-regressed models wildly overstate early six-and-one records.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Right. When you blend Empirical-Bayes regressed team power ratings with net offensive and defensive EPA, strength of schedule, and official NFL Rulebook multi-club tiebreakers, the 6-1 49ers project for 12 wins—giving San Francisco a 93 percent playoff probability, 82.6 percent odds to win the NFC West, and a calibrated 34.5 percent shot at the number-one seed bye, just ahead of 6-1 Minnesota at 29.6 percent and 6-2 Chicago at 15.1 percent. That Week 11 neutral-site showdown against Minnesota in Mexico City is the single biggest swing game in the conference.

sharedAnalyses.title: 2026 Trade Window & Calibrated 10,000-Run Playoff Blueprint: Ranked Needs, Rental Math, -$31.54M 2027 Cap Horizon & 34.5% #1 Bye Odds
sharedAnalyses.markdown:
### 1. Midseason CBA Purchasing Power vs. 2027 Cap & Draft Reality
* **9/18ths Proration Purchasing Power**: Acquiring teams absorb only the remaining **9/18ths** of a player's 2026 base salary while signing/option bonus proration stays on the seller's cap. With **`$35.16M`** in 2026 Top-51 space, San Francisco holds **>`$65M` in annualized base-salary purchasing power** and does **not** need sellers to eat 2026 salary.
* **The True Front-Office Constraints**:
  1. **`-$31.54M` Projected 2027 Cap Deficit** (on an estimated `$327.0M` ceiling): Every 2026 dollar spent reduces 1-for-1 CBA Article 13 rollover needed for 2027 compliance.
  2. **6 Total 2027 Draft Picks**: After trading SF's own 2027 4th-rounder to Indianapolis for **DeForest Buckner**, San Francisco owns **Rd 1 (#31), Rd 2 (#63), Rd 3 (#95), Rd 5 (#170), Rd 6 (#193 via BAL), and Rd 7 (#245 via KC)**—leaving a 75-pick gap between #95 and #170.

### 2. Verified Ranked Needs, Targets & Traps to Avoid
1. **Perimeter WR / 12-Personnel Move TE (Critical)**: With Ricky Pearsall (Season-Ending IR), Christian Kirk (IR — Meniscus), and De'Zhaun Stribling (IR — Ankle) on Injured Reserve, Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. ruled Out on the active roster, and Brandon Aiyuk on Reserve/Left Squad, top cost-controlled fits are **Adonai Mitchell** (NYJ, `~$0.79M` prorated), **Josh Downs** (IND, `~$1.72M`), **Rashod Bateman** (BAL), and **Greg Dulcich** (MIA, `~$0.60M` expiring). *Note on **Quentin Johnston** (LAC): viable only if LAC restructures/retains his guaranteed `$18.0M` 2027 5th-year option.*
2. **Left Guard Pass Protection (High)**: Upgrade interior anchor next to **Trent Williams** via rookie-scale **Kingsley Suamataia** (KC, `~$0.65M` prorated).
3. **Rotational Speed EDGE & Dime DB (Targeted Rentals)**: Expiring one-year rentals on 0-7 LAC—**Khalil Mack** (`$4.0M` prorated, `$0` in 2027) and **Donte Jackson** (`$3.0M` prorated)—or **Jessie Bates III** (ATL, played under DC **Raheem Morris** in 2024–2025, contract voids after 2026).
* **Traps to Reject**: Zero-sack age-37 edge **Cameron Jordan** (0.0 sacks in 7 games), recently extended **Michael Mayer** (LV 3-yr/`$45M` deal), and burning Day-2 picks (#63/#95) on contender starters.

### 3. Calibrated 10,000-Run Playoff Probabilities (Why SF Sits at `34.5%` for the #1 Bye)
* **Empirical-Bayes + Net EPA + SOS Calibration**: Shrinking 7-game sample variance toward league priors (`gp / (gp + 9.5)`) with per-game posterior uncertainty and full NFL Section 16 multi-club tiebreakers places the **6-1** 49ers at **`12` projected wins**, **`93%` Playoff Berth**, **`82.6%` NFC West Title**, and **`34.5%` #1 Seed First-Round Bye**—leading **Minnesota (`6-1`, `29.6%`)** and **Chicago (`6-2`, `15.1%`)** entering the pivotal Week 11 neutral-site H2H clash vs. Minnesota in Mexico City.

sharedAnalyses.title: Scheme & EPA Deep Dive: How DC Raheem Morris, DeForest Buckner & Osa Odighizuwa Transform Nick Bosa’s Pass-Rush Geometry
sharedAnalyses.markdown:
### Executive Finding
Under Defensive Coordinator **Raheem Morris**, pairing **DeForest Buckner** (6'7", 295 lbs, 34.4" arm length) and **Osa Odighizuwa** inside with **Nick Bosa** and **Keion White** on the Wide-9 rails eliminates the #1 protection adjustment offenses used against San Francisco in 2024–2025: **5-man half-slide + RB chip toward Bosa**.

### Key Quantitative & Film Mechanics
1. **Interior Slide Conflict (2i / 3-Tech Split)**:
   * When Morris aligns Buckner at the 3-technique weak and Odighizuwa at the 2i/shade strong, the opposing center must turn toward Odighizuwa or risk immediate A-gap penetration in the quarterback's lap (2.4s pocket collapse).
   * If the center slides away from Buckner + Bosa's side, the offensive guard is left on an island against Buckner's forklift bull-rush, preventing the guard from widening to help the tackle on **T-E (Tackle-End) stunts**.
2. **Early-Down Run-Fit Integrity & Disguised Split-Safety Rotations**:
   * Through Week 7 without Bosa for 5 games, SF relied heavily on **Fred Warner** erasing leaky B-gap creases. Buckner's career tackle-for-loss rate against outside zone restores two-gap knock-back, letting Morris spin two-high shells into late Cover-3 Buzz and Quarters robbers behind a dominant 4-man rush.
3. **Snap-Count Pitch Count Projection (Week 9 vs. Raiders)**:
   * Expect Bosa around **42–46 snaps (~68%)**, with **Mykel Williams**, **Keion White**, and 3rd-round rookie **Romello Height** rotating on early run downs and 2nd-and-long speed rushes.

sharedAnalyses.title: Brock Purdy 2026 Through 7 Games: Why +4.25% CPOE & 3.2% Sack Avoidance Sustain Top-3 NFL Offense
sharedAnalyses.markdown:
### 2026 Statistical Snapshot (6-1 Record)
* **Passing Efficiency**: `146/211 (69.2%)`, `1,748 Yards (8.28 YPA)`, `15 TD`, `4 INT`
* **Total Passing EPA**: `+63.23` (plus `+14.38` rushing EPA on `161` scramble/zone-read yards)
* **Completion % Over Expected (CPOE)**: `+4.25%`
* **Sacks Taken**: Only `7 sacks` across `218 dropbacks` (`3.2% sack rate`)

### What Changed on Film in 2026
1. **Faster Backside Checkdowns vs. Simulated Pressures**: Rather than hunting low-percentage hero throws when two-high shells bracket the deep over route, Purdy has slashed his pressure-to-sack conversion by hitting **Christian McCaffrey** and **George Kittle** on hot option/angle outlets within `3s`.
2. **Anticipation Window Between the Numbers (10–19 Air Yards)**: Even with Brandon Aiyuk on Reserve/Left Squad, Ricky Pearsall on season-ending IR since August, Christian Kirk on IR, and veteran wideouts Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. missing time, Purdy has sustained elite intermediate efficiency (`85` passing first downs) by trusting **Brandin Cooks**, **Jordan Watkins**, and **Jacob Cowing** before they clear linebacker leverage.
